cases.summary: After Ne4, Black's knight on e4 now targets White's knight on g3. After Ne4, Bxe4 is the stronger tested reply than Qe2. In the Ne4 line: The recorded continuation is Bxe4 dxe4. Bxe4 captures the black knight on e4. dxe4 recaptures the white bishop on e4. After Bxe4, Black's pawn on d5 now targets White's bishop on e4. After Bxe4, Black's queen on e6 now targets White's bishop on e4. After Bxe4, Black's pawn on f5 now targets White's bishop on e4. After dxe4, Black's pawn on e4 now targets White's queen on d3. The exchange leaves Black's pawn on e4 blocking the line from Black's queen on e6 to White's pawn on e3. The advanced piece has gone, but the recapturing pawn keeps that pressure closed. In the Ne4 line: The recorded continuation is Qe2 Ncd6. Ncd6 moves the knight out of the attack from White's queen on e2. After Ncd6, Black's knight on d6 supports Black's knight on e4. The recorded continuation is Ng4 Kg1 Nd6 Nf1 Ne4 Rb2 Kh7 Bxe4 dxe4. Bxe4 captures the black knight on e4. dxe4 recaptures the white bishop on e4. Ng4 preserves the original f6 knight while another can be offered on e4. Here Ne4 uses the knight originally on c4, leaving the knight from f6 for Ng4. After dxe4, from g4 it attacks White's pawn on e3 and White's pawn on h2, retaining another source of pressure on the pawn. The immediate Ne4 exchange gives up that piece and this way of continuing the pressure. The compared root choices are g6 and Ne4.
cases.core_semantic_review: pass against the unchanged preregistered minimum

cases.summary: After g5, White's pawn on g5 now targets Black's pawn on h6. After g5, Rfb8 and hxg5 are competitive replies. In the g5 line: The recorded continuation is Rfb8 Ne2. In the g5 line: The recorded continuation is hxg5 hxg5. hxg5 captures the white pawn on g5. hxg5 recaptures the black pawn on g5. After hxg5, White's pawn on f4 now targets Black's pawn on g5. After hxg5, White's pawn on h4 now targets Black's pawn on g5. g5 blocks the forward advance of Black's pawn on g6. The advance makes the pawn structure a choice: taking and recapturing opens the h-file by removing its pawns. With h5, the opponent keeps that file closed: Black's pawn on h5 is blocked by White's pawn on h4 and remains a target of White's bishop on f3. The exchange gives up that pawn target in return for the open file; the closed branch keeps it. In the g5 line: With Nxg5, the black knight originally on h7 captures the white pawn originally on h4. The compared root choices are g5 and Rf2. In the g5 line: fxg5 recaptures the black knight on g5.
cases.core_semantic_review: pass against the unchanged preregistered minimum

interpretation.existing: The final root numerical comparison is g6/Ne4. The unrestricted same-depth root survey also supplied Ng4 Kg1 Nd6 Nf1 Ne4 Rb2 Kh7 Bxe4 dxe4. It trades the original c4 knight and keeps the original f6 knight on g4 targeting e3/h2. This is the preregistered allowed alternative realization, not the exact book Nd5/e3/f4 line; its value is not copied into the selected g6 comparison.
interpretation.fresh: Rfb8 is the tested first-reply leader, competitive with hxg5. The same owned full reply pool supplies h5 as the structurally distinct closed branch. No forced h5, sacrifice, forced win or immediate rook entry is claimed. Nxg5 and fxg5 prices remain in basic prose.
